lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Numbers follows Israel from Sinai through the wilderness: the census, camp and Levites, departure from Sinai, the rebellion at Kadesh and forty years of wandering, Balaam, a second census, and preparation on the plains of Moab for entering the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of where Israel starts and ends in Numbers?
ev: Describe the journey in Numbers in three stages: at Sinai, wandering, and on the plains of Moab.

nodes.d: Numbers 1 records the LORD telling Moses to number all men twenty years old and up able to go to war, with a leader from each tribe, giving a total of 603,550, while the Levites are not counted but appointed over the tabernacle.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who was counted in the first census and who was left out?
ev: Say who was counted and who was not counted, and why the Levites were set apart (1:47-53).
Name the leader role given to one man from each tribe.

nodes.d: Numbers 2 arranges the tribes in four groups around the tabernacle, each under its standard (Judah east, Reuben south, Ephraim west, Dan north), with the Levites' camp in the middle on the march.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Israel camped around the tabernacle?
ev: Say which tribe camped on each side of the tabernacle.
Say where the Levites' camp travelled (2:17).

nodes.t: The Levites take the place of the firstborn
nodes.d: Numbers 3 lists the sons of Aaron (noting Nadab and Abihu died) and the Levite families Gershon, Kohath and Merari with their camp positions, and says the LORD takes the Levites instead of Israel's firstborn, with redemption money for the extra firstborn.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the Levites are given to the LORD in place of the firstborn?
ev: Name the three Levite families and where each camped.
Explain why the LORD says the Levites are his (3:12-13).
Say how the 273 extra firstborn were redeemed (3:46-51).

nodes.t: The work of the Levite families
nodes.d: Numbers 4 counts the Levites aged thirty to fifty and assigns the work of carrying the tabernacle: the Kohathites the holy things after Aaron's sons cover them, the Gershonites the curtains, and the Merarites the boards and pillars.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what each of the Levite families carried when the camp moved?
ev: Say what each Levite family carried.
State the warning about the Kohathites seeing the holy things (4:15, 20).

nodes.t: Uncleanness and restitution in the camp
nodes.d: Numbers 5:1-10 commands that lepers and those with discharges or who touched the dead be put outside the camp, and that someone who wrongs another confesses and repays the wrong plus a fifth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the camp had to be kept clean according to Numbers 5:3?
ev: Name who was sent outside the camp and the reason given in 5:3.
Say what a wrongdoer must do when guilty (5:6-8).

nodes.d: Numbers 5:11-31 prescribes what a husband who suspects his wife of unfaithfulness without witnesses does: bring her to the priest with an offering, have her swear an oath, and drink the water of bitterness, with the result left to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the law of jealousy and say what it is meant to settle?
ev: Say who conducts the ritual and what the woman is made to drink.
Describe the two outcomes the text gives (5:27-28).

nodes.d: Numbers 6:1-21 sets the rules for a man or woman who takes a vow of separation to the LORD: no wine or grape product, no razor, no contact with the dead, and offerings and shaving of the head when the days are ended.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what a Nazirite promised and how the vow ended?
ev: List the three things a Nazirite avoided.
Describe what happens when the vow period ends (6:13-20).

nodes.d: Numbers 6:22-27 gives the words with which Aaron and his sons are to bless Israel in the LORD's name: that the LORD bless and keep them, make his face shine on them and be gracious, and lift up his countenance and give peace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the priestly blessing asks the LORD to do for his people?
ev: Say the three lines of the blessing in your own words.
Say what the LORD promises in 6:27 when the priests put his name on Israel.

nodes.d: Numbers 7 records the twelve tribal princes giving wagons and oxen to the Levites and each bringing the same offering on his own day for the dedication of the altar, and ends with the LORD speaking to Moses from above the mercy seat.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the twelve princes did and what Moses heard at the end of chapter 7?
ev: Say who gave wagons and oxen and which Levite family received none (7:7-9).
Say what the same offering each prince brought included.
Find where the LORD spoke to Moses (7:89).

nodes.t: The lamps and the cleansing of the Levites
nodes.d: Numbers 8 has Aaron set up the seven lamps of the lampstand, then Moses cleanse the Levites by sprinkling, shaving and washing, and Aaron present them as a wave offering in place of the firstborn, with service limited to ages twenty-five to fifty.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Levites were set apart for their work?
ev: Describe how the Levites were cleansed and presented.
Say the ages for active Levite service.

nodes.t: The Passover at Sinai and the second Passover
nodes.d: Numbers 9:1-14 records Israel keeping the Passover in the wilderness and the LORD granting those unclean through a dead body or on a journey a second Passover in the second month.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the provision for the second Passover?
ev: Say why some men could not keep the Passover on time (9:6-7).
Describe what the LORD allowed them to do.

nodes.d: Numbers 9:15-23 says that on the day the tabernacle was set up a cloud covered it, fire by night, and Israel camped or travelled at the LORD's command as the cloud stayed or lifted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel knew when to move and when to stay?
ev: Say what Israel did when the cloud lifted and when it stayed.

nodes.t: The silver trumpets and leaving Sinai
nodes.d: Numbers 10 commands two silver trumpets for assembling and moving the camps, then records that on the twentieth day of the second month the cloud lifted and Israel set out from Sinai in the order of the tribes, with Moses asking Hobab to guide them and a prayer when the ark set out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Israel set out from Sinai?
ev: List the uses of the silver trumpets.
Say which tribe went first and what Moses said when the ark set forward (10:35).

nodes.t: Complaining at Taberah and craving meat
nodes.d: Numbers 11:1-15 tells of the people complaining so that fire burns at the edge of the camp, then the mixed multitude craving the food of Egypt and weeping over the manna, and Moses crying to the LORD that the burden of the people is too heavy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the people wanted and how Moses felt?
ev: Say what the people complained about and what Moses said to the LORD.

nodes.t: The seventy elders and the quail
nodes.d: Numbers 11:16-35 tells how the LORD has Moses gather seventy elders on whom he puts some of the Spirit, Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp and Moses wishes all the LORD's people were prophets, then the LORD sends quail and a plague strikes those who lusted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD answered Moses' complaint and the people's craving?
ev: Retell how the elders were chosen and what happened to them.
Say what happened while the meat was still between their teeth (11:33).

nodes.t: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses
nodes.d: Numbers 12 tells how Miriam and Aaron criticize Moses, the LORD defends him as faithful in all his house and speaks to him mouth to mouth, Miriam becomes leprous, and Moses prays for her and she is shut out seven days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD said about Moses in Numbers 12:6-8?
ev: Say what Miriam and Aaron said and how the LORD described Moses.
Describe the outcome for Miriam and how Moses responded.

nodes.d: Numbers 13 tells how Moses sends one man from each tribe to search Canaan, they return after forty days with a cluster of grapes from Eshcol, and ten give a bad report while Caleb urges them to go up at once.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the report of the spies and the difference between Caleb and the ten?
ev: Say what the spies brought back and what Caleb said.
Tell how the ten described the people of the land.

nodes.t: Israel refuses to enter the land
nodes.d: Numbers 14:1-25 records the people weeping and wishing to return to Egypt, Joshua and Caleb urging faith, the glory of the LORD appearing, Moses interceding with appeal to the LORD's mercy, and the LORD pardoning yet declaring that those who tested him will not see the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the people responded to the spies' report and how Moses prayed?
ev: Say what Joshua and Caleb told the people (14:7-9).
Describe Moses' prayer and the LORD's answer (14:13-23).

nodes.d: Numbers 14:26-45 records the LORD's sentence that the adults who murmured will die in the wilderness, their children will enter, the spies who gave a bad report die by plague, and the people who then presume to go up are beaten by the Amalekites and Canaanites.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israel wandered forty years and who would enter the land?
ev: Say how long the wandering would last and why (14:33-34).
Describe what happened to those who went up anyway (14:44-45).

nodes.t: Offerings for the land and sins of ignorance
nodes.d: Numbers 15:1-31 gives offerings of flour, oil and wine for sacrifices in the land to come, the first of the dough as a heave offering, one law for native and stranger, atonement for sins of ignorance, and the cutting off of the person who sins presumptuously.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the difference the chapter draws between ignorance and presumption?
ev: Say what the section promises (it begins "when ye be come into the land").
Describe the difference between sin through ignorance and a presumptuous sin (15:27-31).

nodes.t: The man who gathered sticks on the sabbath
nodes.d: Numbers 15:32-36 tells of a man found gathering sticks on the sabbath, put in ward until the LORD says he is to be stoned outside the camp by the congregation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the man who gathered sticks and why Moses first waited?
ev: Say what the man did and what the LORD told Moses to do.

nodes.d: Numbers 15:37-41 commands Israel to make fringes with a blue cord on the corners of garments, to look on them and remember all the LORD's commandments and be holy, since the LORD brought them out of Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israelites wore fringes on their garments?
ev: Say what the fringes were for (15:39-40).

nodes.d: Numbers 16:1-35 tells how Korah, Dathan, Abiram and 250 leaders oppose Moses and Aaron, Moses calls for a test with censers, and the earth swallows Korah's company while fire consumes the 250.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Korah's rebellion was about and what happened?
ev: Say what Korah's group claimed (16:3) and how Moses answered (16:5-11).
Describe how the LORD answered the challenge (16:31-35).

nodes.d: Numbers 16:36-50 records the censers beaten into a covering for the altar, the congregation murmuring against Moses and Aaron, a plague killing 14,700, and Aaron running with a censer between the dead and the living to make atonement.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Aaron stopped the plague?
ev: Say what was done with the censers and what Aaron did to stop the plague.

nodes.d: Numbers 17 tells how each tribe's leader lays a rod before the LORD, Aaron's rod for Levi buds, blossoms and yields almonds, and it is kept before the testimony as a sign against rebels, while Israel cries that they will all perish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the budding rod showed and why it was kept?
ev: Say how the rods were used to show whom the LORD had chosen.
Say where Aaron's rod was kept and why (17:10).

nodes.t: Duties and portions of priests and Levites
nodes.d: Numbers 18 charges Aaron and his sons to bear the sanctuary's guilt, assigns the Levites to help while no stranger may come near, gives the priests the offerings and firstborn, and gives the Levites the tithe as their inheritance, from which they give a tithe to the priests.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the priests and Levites were supported?
ev: Say what the priests received and what the Levites received.
Find the reason the Levites have no land (18:20-24).

nodes.t: The red heifer and the water of separation
nodes.d: Numbers 19 prescribes a red heifer without blemish burned outside the camp with cedar, hyssop and scarlet, the ashes mixed with water to sprinkle on the third and seventh days those made unclean by a dead body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the water of separation was for?
ev: Describe how the ashes were prepared and when they were sprinkled.
Say what uncleanness the water was for (19:11-13).

nodes.t: Water from the rock at Meribah
nodes.d: Numbers 20:1-13 tells how Miriam dies at Kadesh, the people quarrel with Moses for lack of water, and the LORD tells Moses to speak to the rock but Moses strikes it twice, and the LORD says Moses and Aaron did not believe him to sanctify him before Israel and will not bring the congregation in.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Moses did wrong at Meribah and what it cost him?
ev: Say what the LORD told Moses to do and what Moses did.
State the consequence given in 20:12.

nodes.d: Numbers 20:14-29 records Israel asking the king of Edom to pass through and being refused, then Aaron's garments passing to Eleazar on mount Hor where Aaron dies and Israel mourns thirty days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the priesthood passed from Aaron to Eleazar?
ev: Say what Moses asked of Edom and the answer.
Describe what happened to Aaron's garments and why (20:24-28).

nodes.t: Victory over Arad, Sihon and Og
nodes.d: Numbers 21:1-3 and 21:10-35 recount Israel's vow and victory over the Canaanite king of Arad, the journey to the plains of Moab, and defeats of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, with Israel taking their lands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the kings Israel defeated and what the LORD said about Og?
ev: Say which two kings Israel defeated after Edom refused passage.
Say what the LORD told Moses about Og (21:34).

nodes.t: The fiery serpents and the bronze serpent
nodes.d: Numbers 21:4-9 tells how the people speak against God and Moses, the LORD sends fiery serpents, the people confess, and Moses makes a bronze serpent on a pole so that anyone bitten who looks at it lives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the bronze serpent and say what the people had to do to live?
ev: Say what the people said, what the LORD sent, and how those bitten were healed.

nodes.d: Numbers 22:1-21 tells how Israel camps on the plains of Moab, Balak king of Moab fears them and sends elders with rewards to Balaam to curse Israel, and God tells Balaam not to go and not to curse them, then permits him to go with the men if they call him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Balak sent for Balaam and what God told him?
ev: Say why Balak wanted Balaam and what God told Balaam first (22:12).

nodes.d: Numbers 22:22-41 tells how the angel of the LORD stands in Balaam's way, the donkey turns aside three times, the LORD opens its mouth and then Balaam's eyes, and the angel tells him to go with the men but speak only what the LORD says; Balak then takes him up to the high places of Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Balaam's journey with the donkey and the angel?
ev: Say what the donkey saw that Balaam did not.
State what the angel told Balaam to speak (22:35).

nodes.d: Numbers 23 records Balaam building seven altars and, with a word put in his mouth by the LORD, blessing Israel twice instead of cursing: how can he curse whom God has not cursed, and God is not a man that he should lie or repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Balaam blessed Israel and what Numbers 23:19 says about God?
ev: Say what Balak wanted and what Balaam said instead (23:8, 20).
Find what 23:19 says about God.

nodes.t: Balaam's third and fourth oracles: a star out of Jacob
nodes.d: Numbers 24 records Balaam blessing Israel a third time, Balak's anger, and a fourth oracle about what will happen in the latter days: a star out of Jacob and a sceptre out of Israel who will have dominion, then short sayings about Edom, Amalek, the Kenites and Asshur.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Balaam said would come out of Jacob in Numbers 24:17-19?
ev: Say what Balak did when Balaam kept blessing Israel (24:10).
Read 24:17-19 and say what is described coming from Jacob.

nodes.d: Numbers 25 tells how Israel at Shittim joins in the worship of Baal of Peor and sins with Moabite women, a plague kills 24,000 until Phinehas acts zealously, and the LORD gives him his covenant of peace and an everlasting priesthood and commands Israel to vex the Midianites.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what sin brought a plague at Peor and what Phinehas did?
ev: Say what Israel did at Shittim and how the plague stopped.
Say what the LORD gave Phinehas (25:11-13).

nodes.d: Numbers 26 records the LORD commanding a new numbering on the plains of Moab, giving the family lists and totals of the tribes (601,730 in all besides the Levites) and noting that apart from Caleb and Joshua none was left of those counted at Sinai, as the LORD had said they would die in the wilderness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the second census showed about the LORD's word at Kadesh?
ev: Say why a second census was taken after the plague and how it was used (26:52-56).
Say who was left from the first census (26:64-65).

nodes.d: Numbers 27:1-11 tells how five daughters of Zelophehad ask Moses for their father's inheritance since he had no sons, and the LORD says they speak right and gives a law of inheritance for daughters, brothers and kinsmen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the daughters of Zelophehad came to Moses and what the LORD decided?
ev: Say what the daughters asked and the LORD's answer.

nodes.t: Moses sees the land; Joshua is appointed
nodes.d: Numbers 27:12-23 tells how the LORD tells Moses to see the land from mount Abarim before he dies, Moses asks for a shepherd for the congregation, and the LORD tells him to lay his hand on Joshua, in whom is the Spirit, and set him before Eleazar and the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Joshua was chosen to lead after Moses?
ev: Say why Moses will not enter the land (27:14).
Describe how Joshua was commissioned.

nodes.t: The daily, sabbath, monthly and spring offerings
nodes.d: Numbers 28 specifies the offerings to be made: the continual burnt offering of two lambs daily, doubled on the sabbath, the monthly burnt offerings, and the offerings for Passover, Unleavened Bread and the day of firstfruits.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the continual burnt offering and when extra offerings were added?
ev: Say what was offered each morning and evening.
Name the feasts covered in the second half of the chapter.

nodes.t: The offerings of the seventh month
nodes.d: Numbers 29 specifies the offerings for the feast of trumpets, the day of atonement and the seven days of tabernacles, with a declining number of bullocks each day and a solemn assembly on the eighth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the feasts of the seventh month and what was offered at tabernacles?
ev: Name the three occasions in the seventh month listed here.
Say how the number of bullocks changes over the days of tabernacles.

nodes.d: Numbers 30 says a man must keep his vow, and sets out when a father or husband may allow or void the vow of a daughter or wife on the day he hears it, while the vow of a widow or divorced woman stands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the chapter says about keeping vows to the LORD?
ev: Say how a man's vow differs from the vows in verses 3-15.
State when a father or husband could confirm or cancel a vow.

nodes.d: Numbers 31 records the LORD commanding vengeance on Midian, a thousand from each tribe going out with Phinehas, the kings and Balaam being killed, Moses' anger that the women who caused Israel to sin at Peor were spared, purification of the army and spoil, and the division of the plunder with a tribute to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the reason the text gives for the war on Midian and how the spoil was divided?
ev: Say why the war against Midian was fought (31:2, 16).
Describe how the soldiers and the plunder were purified and divided.

nodes.t: Reuben and Gad ask for land east of the Jordan
nodes.d: Numbers 32 tells how Reuben and Gad, with great herds, ask to settle in Jazer and Gilead, Moses warns them with the example of the spies, and they agree to cross armed with Israel until the land is taken, so Moses gives land to Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the deal Moses made with Reuben and Gad?
ev: Say what Reuben and Gad asked and the condition Moses set.
Say what Moses said would happen if they did not keep their promise (32:23).

nodes.d: Numbers 33:1-49 lists in order the places Israel camped from leaving Rameses to the plains of Moab by the Jordan, recorded by Moses at the LORD's command, with notes on the Passover night, the Red Sea, Aaron's death and king Arad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the list of stages in Numbers 33 is and why it was written?
ev: Say where the list begins and ends.
Find the note on Aaron's death (33:38-39).

nodes.t: Driving out the nations and the borders of the land
nodes.d: Numbers 33:50-56 and chapter 34 tell Israel to drive out the inhabitants and destroy their idols or they will become thorns in their sides, divide the land by lot, and set the borders of Canaan and the names of the men who divide it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the instructions for taking and dividing the land?
ev: Say what Israel was told to do to the inhabitants and the idols and the warning for not doing it (33:52-56).
Name who divides the land (34:17-19).

nodes.t: Cities for the Levites and cities of refuge
nodes.d: Numbers 35 commands that the Levites receive forty-eight cities with pasture lands, six of them cities of refuge where a person who kills unintentionally may flee from the avenger of blood, with rules for murder, witnesses and the high priest's death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose of cities of refuge?
ev: Say how many cities the Levites got and how many were refuge cities.
State how the text tells murder from accidental killing, and what 35:33-34 says about blood and the land.

nodes.d: Numbers 36 tells how the heads of Gilead's families raise a concern that Zelophehad's daughters marrying outside the tribe would move land to another tribe, and the LORD commands that they marry within their father's tribe so that each tribe keeps its inheritance; the daughters do so.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD told Zelophehad's daughters to marry within their tribe?
ev: Say what concern the family heads raised.
Say what the LORD commanded for heiresses (36:6-9) and what the daughters did.

nodes.d: Leviticus gives the LORD's instructions from the tabernacle: the offerings, the consecration of the priests, clean and unclean, the day of atonement, holy living, the feasts, the jubilee, and the blessings and curses of obedience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a one-sentence summary of what Leviticus is about?
ev: Name the main sections of Leviticus (offerings, priests, clean and unclean, atonement, holiness, feasts, jubilee, blessings and curses).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy records Moses' words to Israel on the plains of Moab in the fortieth year: a review of the journey, the ten commandments and the call to love the LORD, the laws for life in the land, the covenant renewal with its blessings and curses, Moses' song and blessing, and his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain where Israel is and what Moses is doing throughout Deuteronomy?
ev: Describe Deuteronomy as Moses' speeches before Israel enters the land and name its main parts.

nodes.t: John: Believe That Jesus Is the Christ
nodes.d: John presents Jesus as the Word made flesh through signs, 'I am' sayings, a farewell discourse, the cross and resurrection, and states that these things are written so readers believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why John wrote his Gospel and how it begins and ends?
ev: State why John says he wrote the book and name some signs or 'I am' sayings.

nodes.d: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night and is told that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born of water and the Spirit; Jesus compares the Spirit to wind and says the Son of man must be lifted up like the serpent Moses lifted so that believers have eternal life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told Nicodemus about being born again?
ev: Say what Jesus told Nicodemus about new birth and being lifted up.

nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?
ev: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2

nodes.t: Warnings from Israel in the wilderness
nodes.d: Paul reminds the Corinthians that Israel passed through the sea and ate and drank spiritual food, yet many fell; he says these things were examples to us, and that God provides a way of escape from temptation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul uses Israel's failures as a warning, and what God promises in 1 Corinthians 10:13?
ev: List the privileges of Israel in 10:1-4 and the sins in 10:7-10
Explain why Paul says these things were written (10:11)
State the promise of 10:13

nodes.d: Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house, but Christ is faithful as a Son over his own house, and believers are that house if they hold fast.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the text says Christ is greater than Moses (3:3-6)?
ev: Compare servant and son in 3:5-6
Say what condition 3:6 states

nodes.t: Do not harden your hearts as in the wilderness
nodes.d: Quoting the warning that God swore the generation that provoked him in the wilderness would not enter his rest, the writer urges them to beware an evil heart of unbelief and to exhort one another daily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to those who came out of Egypt and what warning the writer draws (3:16-19)?
ev: Say why that generation could not enter (3:19)
Describe what 3:12-13 tells the readers to do

nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)

nodes.d: 2 Peter is a letter from Simon Peter urging growth in the knowledge of Christ, warning against false teachers and scoffers, and pointing to the certain day of the Lord and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 2 Peter warns about and what it tells believers to do?
ev: Name the three sections: growth, false teachers, the day of the Lord
Say what Peter wants believers to remember

nodes.t: The character and end of the false teachers
nodes.d: Peter describes the false teachers as presumptuous, greedy and following Balaam, promising freedom while enslaved to corruption, and says to return to the way of righteousness after knowing it is worse than never knowing it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Peter portrays the false teachers and why turning back is so serious?
ev: Name the charges in 2:13-15
Explain the saying about the dog and the sow in 2:22
Say who Peter compares them to in 2:15-16

nodes.d: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered, warns of ungodly men who crept in, recalls examples of judgment, and ends with a call to keep in God's love and a doxology.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jude asks believers to contend for?
ev: Say who wrote Jude
Say what Jude urges in verse 3

nodes.t: Examples of judgment: unbelievers, angels and Sodom
nodes.d: Jude recalls that the Lord destroyed those who did not believe after saving a people out of Egypt, that angels who left their place are kept in chains until judgment, and that Sodom and Gomorrha suffer the vengeance of eternal fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the three examples of judgment Jude gives?
ev: List the three examples in verses 5-7
Say what Sodom and Gomorrha are set forth as

nodes.t: The ungodly men described: Cain, Balaam, Core and Enoch's prophecy
nodes.d: Jude says these dreamers despise authority, have gone in the way of Cain, the error of Balaam and the rebellion of Core, are like waterless clouds and fruitless trees, and that Enoch prophesied the Lord comes to judge the ungodly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the false men in Jude using the examples and pictures Jude gives?
ev: Say what Jude says about Michael in verse 9
Name the three figures in verse 11
Describe the pictures from nature in verses 12-13
Say what Enoch prophesied in verses 14-15
